changelogHeadings: Rewind shows when you made each edit.
Keep Rewind open without holding Undo.

steps.title: Rewind shows when you made each edit
steps.body: As you scrub Rewind, the readout now shows the real time of day of the edit under the playhead, to the second — for example 3:42:07 PM, Yesterday 3:42:07 PM, or Sep 12 3:42:07 PM. It stays accurate even if you closed PanaLux and came back to the photo later. Edits recorded before this update have no recorded time, so they show none instead of a guess.

steps.title: Keep Rewind open without holding Undo
steps.body: Hold Undo to open Rewind, then press Stop (the square key on the right). Rewind stays open, so you can let go of Undo and use both hands. Press Undo again to close it. Stop still pauses playback as before.

steps.title: What’s New only shows what’s new to you
steps.body: When PanaLux updates it lists the changes since the version you last used, then lights up where each one lives. Someone one update behind sees a short list; someone who skipped several sees more. A feature appears again only if it changed. Help → What’s New… brings this back any time.

steps.title: The Panel Guide opens only when you ask
steps.body: The panel guide no longer appears by itself when PanaLux opens. Open it from the Panel Guide button in the toolbar, or Help → Panel Reference. The intro also plays only the first time, not every launch.

steps.title: Panel lights stay on
steps.body: Your panel's key lights now stay on. Choose how they behave in Settings → Panel → Key lights, and set the Backlight slider there.

steps.title: The intro lights the panel with each scene
steps.body: Each intro scene has its own choreography on the physical panel: a dancing band, the sweep in step with the screen, knob banks counting one-two-three, trackball rings, the held key lighting up, and a chase on the last screen. Help → Watch the Intro, and keep your eyes on the panel.

steps.title: Waves follow your hand
steps.body: Push a trackball and a wave of light travels the way you push it. Turn a knob and one calm ring spreads across the keys beside it. Switch knob waves and the red and green keys on or off in Settings → Panel.

steps.title: A calmer Rewind edge
steps.body: Hold Undo in Lightroom to enter Rewind. The glow along the edge of Lightroom's display is transparent, softly blurred and gently warped, and no longer flickers as you turn the wheel. Nothing changes on your other displays.

steps.title: A calmer Rewind wheel
steps.body: Turn the center ring slowly and each click moves exactly one stop. Faster turns travel further, more gently than before. The Rewind speed dial in Settings still sets how far a hard spin travels.

steps.title: Sync Settings no longer beeps
steps.body: Sync Settings only works when two or more photos are selected in Lightroom. If it is greyed out, PanaLux now says so on screen instead of sending a shortcut that makes the Mac beep. Select several photos in the filmstrip, then press your Sync key.

steps.title: Contact the maker
steps.body: Menu bar → Contact · Bug, Question, Idea, or Settings → Help. Pick a type, write your message and choose Email (private, to panalux@icloud.com) or GitHub (public). Your PanaLux version and connection status are added and nothing is sent until you press send.

steps.title: Hardware color indicators and light show
steps.body: Bypass lights red in Lightroom's Before view and white in After view. Mode keys light green for Offset, Modifiers, Stills, Highlights, Loupe and Masks. In Rewind, Shift Up blinks green with your wheel speed. Help → Play Panel Light Show previews it on your panel.

steps.title: The Panel Guide
steps.body: The Panel Guide button in the toolbar opens your panel reference: every mode, bank and gesture on the real panel drawing, ready to print or save as PDF or PNG. Hold Previous Still and Next Still together on the panel to peek at it while you grade.
